mainTopic: The twenty-אמה height limit for a מבוי's קורה and for סוכה: the אמלתרא (cornice) exception, the idea of noticeability, and a beam or סכך that is partly above twenty.
overview: Earlier on the daf, רב learned the twenty-אמה limit for the קורה of a מבוי from the twenty-אמה doorway of the היכל. The גמרא challenges him: the היכל had אמלתראות (decorative cornices) and was still only twenty high, yet רב is quoted as saying a קורה with an אמלתרא works even above twenty. רב יוסף says the cornice rule is really a ברייתא, but אביי shows that a reliable teacher taught it. רב is then defended in two ways. Either the two ברייתות reflect a מחלוקת תנאים, or, as רב נחמן בר יצחק says, a קורה works because it is noticeable, so a cornice still works high up and the היכל is only a memory aid. The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about height for both סוכה and מבוי, and then gives two definitions of אמלתרא: nest-shaped carvings or valuable cedar poles. Next it asks about a beam or סכך that is partly below and partly above twenty אמות. There are two opposite versions of רבה's ruling, each explained by רבא מפרזקיא and רבינא. Finally the גמרא asks for the practical הלכה: רבה בר רב עולא says both cases are פסול, and רבא says both are כשר, a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A cornice should not help if רב learns from the היכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if רב learns the twenty-אמה limit from the היכל, an אמלתרא should not allow a higher קורה, because the היכל had one and was still only twenty high.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a cornice should not help the beam, because the היכל had a cornice, and even so it was only twenty אמות high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's source. If the היכל doorway is the model, then a cornice should not let the beam be higher than twenty אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב compared the קורה of a מבוי to the היכל doorway, which was twenty אמות high. The challenge says the היכל doorway also had a cornice and still did not go above twenty. So a cornice cannot be a reason to allow more than twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: A decorative carved cornice or molding over a doorway or beam
It should not help or be effective
The Sanctuary, the main inner hall of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the היכל (the Sanctuary, twenty אמות high at its entrance) with the אולם (the Entrance Hall in front of it, forty אמות high at its entrance). The whole back-and-forth depends on this difference.

phrases.english: a cornice should not be effective for it,
phrases.notes: This continues an 'if so' challenge against רב's source from the היכל.

phrases.english: for the Sanctuary had a cornice,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי — עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה הוּא דְּגָבוֹהַּ,
phrases.english: and even so, it was only twenty cubits high,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's source (the היכל doorway), which was taught earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's derivation of the twenty-אמה limit from the היכל doorway
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The model (the היכל) had a cornice and was still limited to twenty. So a cornice cannot justify a beam above twenty.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה of five oak cornices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that there were five oak cornices stacked one above the other over the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: there were five oak cornices above it, one above the other, and another above that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its claim that the היכל had a cornice by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes five oak cornices stacked over the doorway. This is the factual basis for the challenge in Step 1: there were cornices there, yet the height stayed at twenty.

phrases.english: as we learned: five cornices of oak
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מסכת מדות.

phrases.english: were above it,

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ, וְזוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ.
phrases.english: one above the other, and another above that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that backs up the challenge in Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the היכל entrance had cornices
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about five stacked oak cornices

steps.title: Perhaps the cornices were on the Entrance Hall
steps.stepSummary: Someone argues that the משנה may describe the אולם, not the היכל, so it is no refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what refutation is this? Perhaps when that teaching about cornices was taught, it was taught about the אולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the challenge. It suggests the cornices in the משנה were on the אולם, not on the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אולם doorway was forty אמות high, not twenty. If the cornices were only on the אולם, then the היכל (רב's model) may have had no cornice at all. In that case, רב's rule that a cornice changes things is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the refutation? (It is not really a refutation.)
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל

phrases.english: And what refutation is this?
Perhaps when that teaching about cornices was taught,
it was taught about the Entrance Hall?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 2 by reading the משנה as being about a different building.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the היכל had cornices
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer to the אולם, not the היכל

steps.title: The Sanctuary may have been built like the Entrance Hall
steps.stepSummary: The reply: even if the משנה speaks of the אולם, the היכל was probably designed the same way, so it also had cornices.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difficulty is that? Perhaps the design of the היכל was like the design of the אולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against Step 3 and defends the original challenge. It says the היכל probably had cornices just like the אולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the משנה is speaking about the אולם, it is reasonable that both doorways had the same design. So the challenge still stands: the היכל had cornices and was twenty high. This sets up the final, sharper version of the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What difficulty is that? (It is not really a problem.)

phrases.english: And what difficulty is that?
Perhaps the design of the Sanctuary was like the design of the Entrance Hall?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rejection in Step 3, bringing back the original challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that only the אולם had cornices
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The היכל was likely built in the same pattern as the אולם, so it had cornices too

steps.title: רב himself says a cornice allows a beam above twenty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge: רבי אילעא reports that רב said a beam with a cornice works even above twenty אמות. That seems to contradict רב's own source from the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, then, did רבי אילעא say in the name of רב: if the beam is four טפחים wide, even if it is not sturdy, it works. And if it has a cornice, even if it is higher than twenty אמות, one does not need to lower it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its challenge and shows exactly where רב seems to contradict himself. רב allows a cornice to permit a beam above twenty אמות, even though his own model, the היכל, had a cornice and was only twenty high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1–4 established that the היכל, רב's model, had cornices and was still twenty אמות. Now we see רב's actual ruling: a cornice lets the beam be higher than twenty. If he learns from the היכל, that ruling makes no sense, so the challenge is now fully stated.

keyTerms.meaning: To lower or reduce the height

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רב: his model (the היכל) had cornices and was only twenty אמות high, yet רב rules that a cornice lets a קורה be higher than twenty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next move: either explaining רב's ruling or finding a different source for him.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Why, then, did Rabbi Ile'a say that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: רְחָבָה אַרְבָּעָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּרִיאָה.
phrases.english: if it is four handbreadths wide, even though it is not sturdy, it works.
phrases.notes: This is speaking about the קורה (cross beam) of the מבוי.

phrases.english: And if it has a cornice,
even if it is higher than twenty cubits,
one does not need to lower it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the challenge restored in Step 4, the גמרא now states רב's ruling that contradicts it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, reported by רבי אילעא, that a cornice permits a beam above twenty אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own source, the היכל, had cornices and was limited to twenty. So a cornice should not allow more than twenty.

steps.title: The cornice rule is only a ברייתא of unknown authority
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף deflects the challenge. The cornice rule was not said by רב himself. It is a ברייתא, and it is unclear who taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The rule about the cornice is a ברייתא. Who teaches it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on the challenge from step 5. He says רב never said the cornice rule. It comes from a ברייתא, and we do not even know if that ברייתא is reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 5 depended on רב saying two things that clash. If the cornice rule is a separate ברייתא and not רב's own words, then רב does not contradict himself. Asking 'who teaches it?' also suggests that the ברייתא may not be authoritative enough to argue against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A decorative cornice or molding placed on a beam
A ברייתא, a tannaitic teaching outside the משנה
Who teaches it? (questioning the source's reliability)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The cornice rule is a baraita (not Rav's statement),
phrases.notes: So it is not רב contradicting himself.

phrases.english: Who teaches it?
phrases.notes: Implying the source may not be reliable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמלתרא מתניתא היא, מאן קתני לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise of step 5 that רב himself said the cornice rule
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attribution of the cornice rule to רב and questions its authority
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed the cornice rule was רב's own statement, but it is really an unattributed ברייתא

steps.title: A reliable teacher taught it, so the challenge returns
steps.stepSummary: אביי identifies the teacher as חמא בריה דרבה בר אבוה, a reliable source. Even as a ברייתא, the cornice rule still challenges רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: But חמא, the son of רבה בר אבוה, teaches it! So let the cornice rule be a ברייתא, and it still poses a difficulty for רב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's question 'who teaches it?' The answer is a known, trustworthy teacher. So the ברייתא is authoritative, and the problem for רב comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not have to contradict himself for there to be a problem. A reliable ברייתא that clashes with רב's derivation from the היכל is also a valid challenge. So moving the cornice rule from רב to a ברייתא does not remove the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: חמא, son of רבה בר אבוה, a reliable teacher of ברייתות
Let it be a difficulty for רב

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא חָמָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: But Chama son of Rabba bar Avuh teaches it,
phrases.notes: Answers 'who teaches it?' with a reliable source.

phrases.english: so let the cornice rule be a baraita,
and it still poses a difficulty to Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא חמא בריה דרבה בר אבוה קתני לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 6's deflection and brings back the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's derivation of the twenty-אמה limit from the היכל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An authoritative ברייתא allows a cornice beam above twenty, but the היכל had cornices and was only twenty high. So the ברייתא conflicts with רב's source.

steps.title: רב answers: it is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב could reply that the two ברייתות contradict each other even without him. So they must reflect a dispute between תנאים, and רב follows one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: Take me out of this discussion. Do the ברייתות not contradict each other on their own? Whatever you would answer, that it is a dispute between תנאים, I also say it is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. One ברייתא learns the entrance size from the היכל, and the other ברייתא allows a cornice beam above twenty. These clash with each other whether or not רב exists. So they are two opinions of תנאים, and רב simply sides with the opinion that learns from the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not deny the contradiction. It admits that the two ברייתות disagree and explains that disagreement as a מחלוקת תנאים. An אמורא like רב is allowed to follow one תנא against another, so the cornice ברייתא does not refute him.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove me from here (set my opinion aside)
It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the cornice ברייתא is wrong. He is saying it reflects a different תנא's opinion, while he follows the ברייתא that learns from the היכל.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
Remove me from here,
don't the baraitot contradict each other?
phrases.notes: The היכל ברייתא against the cornice ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
It is a dispute between tannaim;
according to me too, it is a dispute between tannaim.
phrases.notes: רב follows one side of that dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לך רב: דל אנא מהכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's renewed challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the conflicting sources to a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות disagree with each other, and רב follows the תנא who learns from the היכל
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common tool across the גמרא. When a source conflicts with an אמורא, it is often enough to show that the source reflects only one side of a disagreement among תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתות agree: the beam is a marker and the היכל is a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתות do not contradict at all. A קורה works because it is noticeable, and a cornice is noticeable even above twenty. The mention of the היכל is only a memory aid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Without רב, the ברייתות do not contradict each other. According to the רבנן, what is the reason a קורה works? Because it serves as a marker. And when the ברייתא says 'more than the entrance of the היכל,' that is only a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different answer. He reconciles the two ברייתות instead of calling them a dispute. The basic rule comes from the beam being noticeable, not from the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain beam above twenty אמות is too high to be noticed, but a cornice catches the eye, so it still works as a marker. The היכל was mentioned only because its doorway happened to be twenty high, which makes the number easy to remember. With that reading, the two ברייתות fit together.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. (1) רב: the ברייתות are a מחלוקת תנאים, and רב follows the היכל derivation. (2) רב נחמן בר יצחק: the reason for a קורה is to be noticeable, so a cornice works above twenty, and the היכל is only a memory aid.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּלָא רַב — מַתְנְיָיתָא אַהֲדָדֵי לָא קַשְׁיָין:
phrases.english: Without Rav, the baraitot do not contradict each other:
According to the Rabbis, what is the reason for a beam?
Because it is a noticeable marker,
phrases.notes: A cornice is noticeable even above twenty.

phrases.english: and that which it teaches, 'more than the entrance of the Sanctuary,'
is merely a mnemonic.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב נחמן בר יצחק אמר: בלא רב מתנייתא אהדדי לא קשיין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 8, reconciling the ברייתות instead of calling them a dispute
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the היכל reference is a memory aid, and the real reason is noticeability
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות contradict each other, so they must reflect a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות agree: a קורה is a marker, a cornice stays noticeable above twenty, and the היכל only helps remember the number

steps.title: Setting up a problem for רב נחמן בר יצחק using רבה's teaching on סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer works only if he does not hold of רבה's teaching. רבה taught that a סוכה above twenty אמות is invalid because the eye does not notice the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רב נחמן בר יצחק: his answer is fine if he does not agree with רבה. But what if he does agree with רבה? רבה said: The verse says, 'So that your generations will know that I made you dwell in סוכות.' Up to twenty אמות, a person knows he is living in a סוכה. Above twenty אמות, a person does not know, because the eye does not catch the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רב נחמן בר יצחק. It first quotes רבה's teaching about סוכה, which will be used in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the twenty-אמה limit for סוכה comes from noticeability. Above twenty אמות, people do not look up, so they do not notice the סכך. This is the same reasoning that רב נחמן בר יצחק used for the מבוי, and that overlap is about to cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: So that your generations will know (ויקרא כג:מג)
The eye catches it / notices it

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished in this step. רבה's teaching is only the setup. The actual question, 'why argue twice?', comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַבָּה,
phrases.english: it works out well if he does not hold this teaching of Rabba,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַבָּה,
phrases.english: but if he does hold this teaching of Rabba, there is a problem.
For Rabba said: It is written:
"So that your generations will know
that I made you dwell in booths".
Up to twenty cubits,
a person knows that he is living in a sukka.
Above twenty cubits,
a person does not know,
because the eye does not catch it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא אִי לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַבָּה, אֶלָּא אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against the תירוץ of רב נחמן בר יצחק in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the מבוי rule is based on noticeability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה already explains the סוכה dispute with noticeability. That sets up the problem of a repeated dispute.

steps.title: Why would the תנאים argue about the same point twice?
steps.stepSummary: If the סוכה dispute is about noticeability, and the מבוי dispute is also about noticeability, then why would the same dispute be taught in two places?
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that with סוכה too, they argue about noticeability. Why do I need them to argue in two places?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the real question. If both disputes are about the same idea, one of them seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about height in both סוכה and מבוי. If both arguments are about whether the eye notices something high up, teaching both looks repetitive. This suggests that the מבוי dispute must be about something else, such as רב's היכל idea, which would undo רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need them to argue in two places?

phrases.english: Evidently, regarding sukka too,
they argue about noticeability.
Why do I need them to argue in two cases?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 10 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation of the מבוי dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dispute would be repeated with no new information, so the מבוי dispute must have a different basis.

steps.title: Both disputes are needed because סוכה and מבוי are used differently
steps.stepSummary: צריכא: from סוכה alone, we might think רבי יהודה agrees about מבוי. From מבוי alone, we might think the רבנן agree about סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had סוכה, I would say רבי יהודה rules leniently only there: a סוכה is for sitting, so the eye eventually catches the roof. But a מבוי is for walking, so I would say he agrees with the רבנן. And if we only had the מבוי case, I would say the רבנן are strict only there, but for סוכה they agree with רבי יהודה. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן בר יצחק. Even if both disputes are about noticeability, each one teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether something is noticeable depends on how a place is used. In a סוכה you sit for a long time, so you are more likely to look up. In a מבוי you just walk through, so you are less likely to look up. The disagreement in each case therefore shows how far each side goes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
It is made for walking through

steps.whatToRemember: Noticeability is not one fixed rule. It depends on use: a place made for sitting gets looked at more than a place made for walking. So both the סוכה dispute and the מבוי dispute are needed, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the directions. With סוכה, the reasoning is that רבי יהודה's leniency is strongest. With מבוי, the reasoning is that the רבנן's strictness is strongest. Each case is the 'easy' case for one side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכותא: two disputes that look the same are each needed, because each case could have pushed one side to agree with the other.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had taught us only regarding sukka,
I would say that in this case Rabbi Yehuda says it is valid,
since it is made for dwelling,
the eye catches it.
But an alleyway, which is made for walking,
I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.
And if it had taught us only in this case (alleyway),
I would say that only in this case do the Rabbis say it is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ אֵימָא מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: but in that case (sukka), I would say they agree with Rabbi Yehuda.
Therefore, it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why argue twice' question of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reasoning, so both are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only one case, we might think the other side agrees in the other case, because of how the place is used (sitting or walking).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both disputes are taught so that we know רבי יהודה is lenient even for a מבוי and the רבנן are strict even for a סוכה.

steps.title: What exactly is an אמלתרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definition of the word אמלתרא, the cornice mentioned earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an אמלתרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question. It wants to define the word אמלתרא, which came up in the ברייתא about a beam with a cornice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, אמלתרא was translated loosely as 'cornice.' Here the גמרא asks what it physically is. This is a word-definition question, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A decorative carving on a beam (cornice)

phrases.english: What is an amaltera?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new side topic, defining a term from the earlier ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical meaning of the word אמלתרא

steps.title: רב חמא בריה דרבה בר אבוה: carvings shaped like birds' nests
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בריה דרבה בר אבוה says an אמלתרא is a carving shaped like birds' nests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא, son of רבה בר אבוה, said: birds' nests (carvings shaped like nests).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer. An אמלתרא is a decorative carving that looks like birds' nests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same חמא בריה דרבה בר אבוה whom אביי named in step 7 as the one who taught the cornice ברייתא. So the person who taught the ברייתא is also the one explaining its word.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חָמָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Chama son of Rabba bar Avuh said:
Birds' nests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָמָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמלתרא means decorative carvings shaped like birds' nests.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they say it means cedar poles
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings a different explanation from ארץ ישראל: an אמלתרא is cedar poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say it means pieces of cedar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second definition from the scholars in ארץ ישראל. An אמלתרא is cedar poles or planks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different picture of the object: pieces of cedar wood instead of nest-shaped carvings. Either way, it is something that makes the beam stand out, which is why it works even above twenty אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There are two definitions of אמלתרא: nest-shaped carvings (רב חמא) or cedar poles (ארץ ישראל). Both describe something on the beam that draws the eye.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
They say in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
Cedar poles.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר, אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative definition to the one in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמלתרא means cedar poles, according to the scholars of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two definitions
steps.stepSummary: The view that says cedar poles would surely also accept birds'-nest carvings. The view that says birds'-nest carvings would not accept cedar poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the cornice means cedar poles would certainly also allow birds'-nest carvings. The one who says it means birds'-nest carvings would not allow cedar poles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what practical difference there is between רב חמא's definition (birds' nests) and רב דימי's definition (cedar poles).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carvings are the more eye-catching option, so whoever accepts plain cedar poles would accept carvings even more (כל שכן). The birds'-nest view, however, accepts only carvings and does not accept cedar poles.

phrases.english: The one who said cedar poles,
all the more so birds' nests.
The one who said birds' nests,
but cedar poles, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר פִּסְקֵי דְאַרְזָא, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן קִינֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two definitions given in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cedar view includes carvings. The carvings view excludes cedar poles.

steps.title: Why would cedar poles make the beam noticeable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the cedar-poles view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says cedar poles, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why plain cedar poles would draw the eye to a beam that is higher than twenty אמות. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carvings are obviously eye-catching, but plain wood is not. So the גמרא needs an explanation for why cedar poles would count.

phrases.english: And the one who said cedar poles,
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר פִּסְקֵי דְאַרְזָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind the definition just discussed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why cedar poles make a high beam noticeable.

steps.title: First answer: the poles are long
steps.stepSummary: Cedar poles are long, and their great length catches the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because its length is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that long cedar poles stand out because of their size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a large, long object catches the eye even when it is placed high up. The next step will test this reason and find a problem with it.

phrases.english: Because its length is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.

steps.title: A סוכה is also long, yet it is still invalid
steps.stepSummary: A סוכה is also long, but the רבנן still say it is פסול above twenty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a סוכה is long too, and the רבנן still say it is not valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'length' answer by pointing to סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being long made something noticeable, then a long סוכה above twenty אמות should be כשר. The רבנן still disqualify it, so length alone cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that...

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the earlier מבוי ruling. Here the גמרא borrows the רבנן's ruling on סוכה to test the logic of the מבוי case.

phrases.english: But a sukka, whose length is great,
and the Rabbis say that it is not valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that length makes something noticeable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: a long סוכה is still פסול above twenty אמות.

steps.title: Better answer: cedar is valuable, so people talk about it
steps.stepSummary: Cedar is important and valuable, so it draws attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since it is valuable, it gets talked about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the length reason and gives a new one: cedar is valuable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Expensive cedar makes people stop and stare, and they point it out to others. So the beam becomes noticeable through its importance, not through its size. A סוכה does not have this quality, so the challenge is resolved.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב דימי, cedar poles work because they are valuable and draw attention, not because they are long.

phrases.english: Rather: since it is valuable,
it has publicity.
phrases.notes: People talk about it and look at it

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כֵּיוָן דְּקָא חֲשִׁיב אִית לֵיהּ קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of step 18.

steps.title: What if part is below twenty and part is above?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a beam or סכך that is partly within twenty אמות and partly above.
steps.simpleTranslation: What if part of the beam is within twenty and part is above twenty, or part of the סכך is within twenty and part is above twenty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a beam or סכך that is split across the twenty-אמה line. This sets up רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each case was either fully below twenty or fully above it. Now the גמרא asks whether the lower part is enough to make the whole thing valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The cross beam over the מבוי

phrases.english: Part of the beam within twenty,
and part of the beam above twenty;
part of the roofing within twenty,
and part of the roofing above twenty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about mixed heights.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of a beam or סכך that is partly above twenty אמות.

steps.title: רבה: valid in a מבוי, invalid in a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that the split case is כשר in a מבוי but פסול in a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: In a מבוי it is valid; in a סוכה it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the split-height question with two different results for the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מבוי, the part that is within twenty אמות is enough. In a סוכה, the part above twenty disqualifies it. The two cases split here even though they looked parallel until now.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first place in the sugya where מבוי and סוכה get different rulings, which raises the question of what makes them different.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
in an alleyway, it is valid;
in a sukka, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בְּמָבוֹי כָּשֵׁר, בְּסוּכָּה פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מבוי is כשר; a סוכה is פסול.

steps.title: Why not 'thin out' the סכך just like the beam?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the reasoning of קלוש, which makes the split beam כשר in a מבוי, does not also make split סכך כשר in a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a מבוי, that it is כשר? It is because we say 'thin it out.' For a סוכה too, let us say 'thin it out'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's distinction from Step 22. It asks why the logic that works for a מבוי should not also work for a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מבוי, we treat the part of the beam above twenty אמות as if it were not there and keep only the lower part. The גמרא asks why we cannot do the same with סוכה roofing: ignore whatever is above twenty and keep the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
Thin it out; treat the part above twenty אמות as if it were removed

steps.confusionAlert: קלוש does not mean anyone physically cuts the beam. It is a legal way of looking at it: we pretend the part above twenty אמות is not there.

phrases.english: What is different about an alleyway, that it is fit,
because we say: 'thin it out'?
phrases.notes: We mentally remove the part above twenty אמות.

phrases.english: For a sukka too, let us say: 'thin it out'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's split ruling from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's distinction between a מבוי and a סוכה in the split case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the מבוי ruling (קלוש) seems to apply just as well to a סוכה, so the two cases should have the same ruling.

steps.title: Thinning the סכך would leave more sun than shade
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that removing the סכך above twenty אמות would leave a סוכה whose sun is more than its shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thin it out, it becomes a סוכה whose sun is more than its shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first explanation of why קלוש cannot work for a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה needs more shade than sun to be כשר. If we mentally remove the upper part of the סכך, the remaining roofing may not give enough shade, so the סוכה would be פסול.

phrases.english: If you thin it out,
it becomes one whose sun is more than its shade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קָלְשַׁתְּ הָוְיָא לַהּ חֲמָתָהּ מְרוּבָּה מִצִּילָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: the result of thinning disqualifies a סוכה but not a מבוי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קלוש should work equally for a סוכה and a מבוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: A thinned סוכה fails the rule of more shade than sun.

steps.title: The beam would also be too weak, so both must be accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. A thinned beam would be flimsy enough for the wind to blow away, yet we still treat it as strong like metal skewers. So we should also treat the thinned סכך as having more shade than sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, if you thin it out, it becomes a beam that the wind can blow away. Rather, you must say they are treated like metal skewers. Here too, you must say the סוכה is treated as having more shade than sun!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 24 by showing the same problem exists in the מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If thinning the beam leaves something too weak, then קלוש should fail in a מבוי too. Since we still accept the מבוי, we must be treating the thinned beam as sturdy, like metal skewers. By the same logic, the thinned סכך should be treated as still giving enough shade.

keyTerms.meaning: Cross beam placed over the entrance of a מבוי
That can be blown away by the wind
Perforce; you are forced to say

phrases.english: Here too, if you thin it out,
it becomes a beam that can be blown away by the wind.
Rather, you are forced to say,
they are treated like metal skewers.
Here too, you are forced to say
it is treated as having more shade than sun!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִי קָלְשַׁתְּ הָוְיָא לַהּ קוֹרָה הַנִּיטֶּלֶת בָּרוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 24 by drawing a parallel.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The sun-versus-shade explanation of רבה's distinction
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same weakness exists in a thinned beam. Since the מבוי overlooks it, the סוכה should overlook its weakness too.

steps.title: One person forgets, but many people remind each other
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא explains the difference practically. A private סוכה owner will not be reminded to fix it if the lower part falls away. In a public מבוי, people remind one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא from פרזקיא said: A סוכה belongs to an individual, so he will not be reminded. A מבוי belongs to the public, so they remind each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזקיא gives a new reason for רבה's ruling. The new reason is based on how people actually behave, not on the logic of קלוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the part below twenty אמות might fall away and leave only the part above twenty. A lone סוכה owner may not notice and would sit in a פסול סוכה. In a shared מבוי, many residents will notice and remind each other to repair it, so חז"ל did not need to be strict there.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the town of פרזקיא

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version of רבה, the split case is כשר in a מבוי but פסול in a סוכה. After the קלוש logic fails, רבא מפרזקיא gives a practical reason: one person can forget, but a public group reminds each other. רבינא gives a second reason in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic distinction can rest on real-world human behavior (who will notice a problem) rather than on formal legal logic.

phrases.english: Rava from Parzakya said:
A sukka, which belongs to an individual, he will not be reminded,
an alleyway, which belongs to the many, they remind each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejection in Step 25, gives a new explanation for רבה's distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction based on private versus public use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference would have to be based on the logic of קלוש, which was shown to apply equally to both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference comes from the risk of forgetting: an individual may not fix the problem, but a public group will remind each other.

steps.title: Torah law is treated strictly, rabbinic law leniently
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the difference this way: סוכה is a Torah law, so רבנן were strict with it. מבוי is a rabbinic law, so רבנן were not strict with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: A סוכה is a Torah law, so the Sages were strict with it. A מבוי is a rabbinic law, so the Sages were not strict with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer to the question from step 23: why does the קלוש reasoning work for a מבוי but not for a סוכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers looked for a physical or practical difference between the two cases. רבינא instead points to the level of the law. For a Torah-level מצוה like סוכה, רבנן refused to rely on the leniency of imagining the סכך thinned. For a beam in a מבוי, which is only required מדרבנן, they allowed that leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah; a Torah-level law
From the Rabbis; a rabbinic-level law

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. רבינא is giving another answer to the same question that רבא מפרזקיא answered in step 26.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version of רבה, there are two reasons why the מבוי is lenient: people remind each other in public (רבא מפרזקיא), and a מבוי is only rabbinic (רבינא).

phrases.english: Ravina said:
A sukka, which is a Torah law —
the Sages were strict with it;
an alleyway, which is rabbinic —
the Sages were not strict with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the step 23 question, parallel to רבא מפרזקיא's practical answer in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by the source of the law (Torah versus rabbinic)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קלוש reasoning should apply equally to a סוכה and a מבוי
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן applied the leniency only to the rabbinic מבוי, not to the Torah-level סוכה

steps.title: A reversed version of רבה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה taught רבה's ruling the opposite way: the split case is פסול in a מבוי and כשר in a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה taught this teaching of רבה the opposite way. רבה said: In a מבוי it is invalid; in a סוכה it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבה's ruling that flips the outcome. This sets up a new round of questions on the reversed version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the split beam helped a מבוי but the split סכך did not help a סוכה. Here the results are swapped. Because of this, the back-and-forth arguments that follow will also run in the opposite direction.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions together. In this version the סוכה is the lenient case and the מבוי is the strict case.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana
taught this teaching of Rabba in the opposite way.
Rabba said:
in an alleyway, it is invalid;
in a sukka, it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה מַתְנֵי לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַבָּה אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a competing version of the ruling from step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The split case is פסול in a מבוי and כשר in a סוכה

steps.title: Why not apply the thinning logic to the beam too?
steps.stepSummary: If the סוכה is כשר because we imagine the upper סכך thinned away, the same reasoning should make the beam in a מבוי כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes a סוכה different, that it is valid? Because we say: imagine it thinned. So in a מבוי too, let us say: imagine it thinned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reversed version: the reasoning that makes the סוכה כשר seems to work just as well for the מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the סוכה is כשר because we treat the סכך above twenty אמות as if it were removed. The same move could be made with the part of the beam above twenty אמות. So why is the מבוי פסול?

keyTerms.meaning: Thin it; treat the part above twenty אמות as if it were removed

phrases.english: What is different about a sukka, that it is valid?
Because we say: thin it.
In an alleyway too, let us say: thin it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversed ruling from step 28; it mirrors the question of step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the split beam is פסול in a מבוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קלוש reasoning that makes the סוכה כשר should equally make the מבוי כשר

steps.title: A thinned beam would blow away in the wind
steps.stepSummary: If you imagine the beam thinned, it becomes a flimsy beam that the wind can carry off, so it cannot count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thin it, it becomes a beam that can be blown away by the wind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the thinning logic does not work for the beam, because the remaining thin beam would be too weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam for a מבוי must be sturdy enough to stay in place. Once we imagine the part above twenty אמות removed, what is left is weak enough to be blown away. So it cannot serve as a valid beam.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam that the wind can carry off

phrases.english: If you thin it,
it becomes a beam that is carried off by the wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קְלַשַׁת, הָוֵי לַהּ קוֹרָה הַנִּיטֶּלֶת בְּרוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29; it mirrors the answer of step 24 in reverse
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a physical defect that appears only in the מבוי case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thinning should work for the beam just as it does for the סכך
steps.terutzMaskana: A thinned beam is too flimsy to count

steps.title: If thinned סכך still gives shade, a thinned beam is still sturdy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. Thinned סכך would also let in more sun than shade, yet we still treat it as giving more shade. So we should likewise treat the thinned beam as being as strong as metal skewers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, if you thin the סכך, it becomes a סוכה whose sun is more than its shade! Rather, you must say that it is treated as having more shade than sun. Here too, you must say that the thinned beams are treated like metal skewers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 30 by showing that the same problem exists in the סוכה, and we ignore it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we really imagined the upper סכך removed, the סוכה would be left with more sun than shade, and that is פסול. Since the סוכה is still כשר, we must treat the thinned סכך as still giving enough shade. By the same logic, the thinned beam should be treated as strong, like thin metal skewers that do not blow away. So the difference between the cases is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Its sun is more than its shade (this makes a סוכה פסול)
Its shade is more than its sun (this makes a סוכה כשר)
You are forced to say; necessarily
Metal skewers: thin, yet strong and stable

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same argument as step 25, but turned around. There, the beam was the accepted case and was used to challenge the סוכה. Here, the סוכה is the accepted case and is used to challenge the beam.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the thinning idea cannot be applied to one case and not the other on physical grounds. Some other kind of distinction is still needed.

phrases.english: Here too, if you thin it —
it becomes a sukka whose sun is more than its shade!
Rather, you are forced to say
it is treated as having more shade than sun;
here too, you are forced to say
they are treated like metal skewers!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִי קָלְשַׁתְּ — הָוְיָא לַהּ חֲמָתָהּ מְרוּבָּה מִצִּילָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 30 by showing the same weakness in the סוכה case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סוכה case has the same weakness after thinning (more sun than shade), yet we accept the thinned סכך anyway; so the beam should be accepted too

steps.title: One owner remembers, many owners forget
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא explains the second version: a סוכה belongs to one person, who will remember to check it, while a מבוי belongs to many people, who rely on each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא from פרזקיא said: A סוכה belongs to one person. He puts the responsibility on himself and remembers to fix it. A מבוי belongs to many people. They rely on one another, and nobody remembers to fix it.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 31 knocked down the 'thinning' answer. Now the גמרא gives a brand-new reason why, in רב אדא בר מתנה's version, the סוכה is כשר but the מבוי is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is about people, not about the structure itself. One owner of a סוכה will make sure it is fixed, so רבנן could be lenient. In a shared מבוי everyone assumes someone else will lower the beam, so רבנן were strict to make sure it really gets done.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the town of פרזקיא, a different person from the famous רבא
he puts it on himself, meaning he takes responsibility

phrases.english: Rava from Parzakya said:
A sukka, which belongs to an individual,
he places it upon himself and is reminded;
phrases.notes: He takes responsibility and remembers to fix the problem.

phrases.english: an alleyway, which belongs to many,
they rely on each other and are not reminded,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 31 with a new reason for the version in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical, human-behavior distinction between private and shared responsibility
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the thinning logic should work for both, the סוכה and the מבוי should have the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference comes from who is responsible. A private owner remembers to fix things, but shared owners neglect them, so רבנן were strict only in the מבוי.

steps.title: The partners' pot proverb
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא supports his point with a popular saying: a pot owned by partners ends up neither hot nor cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As people say: a pot that belongs to partners is neither hot nor cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the 'many owners forget' idea with a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each partner thinks the other one will tend the pot, so in the end nobody does it properly. That is exactly what happens with the shared beam of a מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: as people say, introducing a popular proverb

phrases.english: as people say:
a pot belonging to partners
is neither hot nor cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of step 32 with a folk proverb.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that shared responsibility leads to neglect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular folk saying about a partners' pot

steps.title: A rabbinic law needs extra strengthening
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the second version differently: a סוכה is a Torah law and needs no extra reinforcement, while a מבוי is a rabbinic law and does need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: A סוכה is a Torah law, so it does not need extra strengthening. A מבוי is a rabbinic law, so it needs extra strengthening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second reason for רב אדא בר מתנה's version, where the סוכה is כשר and the מבוי is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People already take Torah laws seriously, so רבנן did not need to add strictness for a סוכה. People tend to treat rabbinic laws lightly, so רבנן made the מבוי rules stricter to protect them.

keyTerms.meaning: from the Torah, a Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: In step 27, רבינא used the same Torah-versus-rabbinic split to reach the opposite result: Torah law gets more strictness. Here, in the other version of רבה, he argues that the rabbinic law is the one that needs strengthening. Both arguments are logical. Each one simply fits a different version of רבה's ruling.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
A sukka, which is by Torah law, does not require reinforcement.
An alleyway, which is by rabbinic law, requires reinforcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent explanation for the version in step 28, parallel to step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Torah law should always get more strictness than a rabbinic law.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rabbinic law is more likely to be treated lightly, so רבנן reinforced the מבוי rules. The Torah law of סוכה needs no such extra protection.

steps.title: What is the final הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: Since there are two opposite versions of רבה's ruling, the גמרא asks what the final הלכה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is asking for the practical ruling and gets ready to present the opinions that answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions of רבה have been defended, so the explanations alone cannot decide the הלכה. The גמרא now asks directly what the ruling is when part of the סכך or the beam is above twenty אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the two versions to asking for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical הלכה for a סוכה or מבוי where part of the covering is above twenty אמות

steps.title: Both are invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב עולא rules that both the סוכה and the מבוי are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב עולא said: both this one and that one are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer to the question is given: be strict in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב עולא does not split the cases at all. If part of the סכך or part of the beam is above twenty אמות, the whole thing does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: this and that, meaning both cases

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Ulla said:
both this and that are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both the סוכה and the מבוי are פסול.

steps.title: Both are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules the opposite: both the סוכה and the מבוי are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: both this one and that one are כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion answers the same question by being lenient in both cases. רבא's statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא also treats the two cases the same, but in the lenient direction. So neither later authority accepted a split between סוכה and מבוי. They argue only over whether both are פסול or both are כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of רבה split the סוכה and מבוי cases in opposite directions. The practical הלכה drops the split entirely: רבה בר רב עולא says both are פסול, and רבא says both are כשר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
both this and that are fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to the same question as step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both the סוכה and the מבוי are כשר.
